cases.description: The reference device plugin: every required field, no optionals.
Every manifest states its trust model explicitly. hash-only with an empty entries list is the only shape v2 accepts.
The management tier parses the same as the device tier; the difference is which loader refuses it, not what the schema allows.
'*' matches any model or firmware.
A bare token is an exact-match constraint.
Not JSON at all.
Valid JSON, wrong shape.
Unknown top-level fields are rejected, not ignored: the device and the server must never disagree about what a manifest said.
A required field is absent.
payload is required.
kvmd's existing get_plugin_class treats a leading underscore as unknown, so a manifest may not mint one.
Module names are lowercase.
A dash is not valid in a Python module name.
Empty name.
No loader exists for this type.
A security tier is never defaulted.
runtime is required.
Invariant 1: the manifest cannot express a path that escapes the loader root.
Invariant 1: absolute paths are refused.
Invariant 1: backslash separators are refused.
Only Python modules are loadable.
entry must be rooted at plugins/.
Invariant 1: entry's type segment disagrees with type, so placement and description disagree. That is a refusal, never a redirection.
Invariant 1: entry's stem disagrees with name, which would let the manifest name one module and place another.
Canonical means one spelling; uppercase hex is a violation, not something to normalise.
Not 64 hex characters.
Non-hex characters.
An empty bundle is not a plugin.
Negative size.
The receiver must buffer and hash the bundle before it may touch the disk, so an unbounded payload is a memory-exhaustion path the gate cannot cover.
Exactly at the 8 MiB cap is allowed.
sandbox is reserved until a vocabulary exists. Accepting a declaration nothing enforces would be worse than having no field at all.
An explicitly empty sandbox is accepted.
An absent sandbox is accepted.

The old v1 name is now an unknown field. It was renamed because kazbek already uses 'capability' for subject-scoped permission keys, and two vocabularies under one word is a bug waiting to be written.
revision is mandatory.
revision starts at 1.
Negative revision.
A version string is not a revision.
bool is an int subclass in Python; true is not a revision.
A large monotonic counter is fine.
The block is required so every manifest states its trust model explicitly; an absent block would leave 'unsigned' and 'omitted' indistinguishable, which is the ambiguity a downgrade lives in.
A manifest declaring a trust model this implementation does not have is uninterpretable, not merely invalid.
model is required inside the block.
entries is required inside the block.
A v2 implementation cannot check a signature and must not accept a manifest that claims one.
threshold and expires are accepted now so the later models need no schema migration.
Unknown members inside the block are refused like any other.
The v1 stub shape (alg/value/key_id) is no longer the schema.
Only >=, <=, ==, bare token and * parse.
An empty constraint does not parse.

description: Manifest validation vectors. A case with 'raw' supplies the exact bytes to parse; otherwise encode 'manifest' canonically. 'canonical' is the expected canonical JSON encoding and must round-trip byte-stably.
